title: Still early, but are you able to use fable 5.2 as a director for your game dev without burning through your limit in a few minutes?
author: throwaway09234023322
selftext: I'm waiting for my reset to use it but was curious. I'm on the max plan. Anyone able to use it effectively in a workflow? Or is it just for a couple complex prompts and you blow through your limit?

comments.author: Bavariasnaps
comments.body: thanks for the advice gonna try it out

comments.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
comments.body: I just switched over to fable last night to test it out. I'd never used fable before. I've got mine set up with instructions to only use opus 5.5 medium and sonnet as helpers, and it reviews everything that they do. My instructions are also set to reduce charge so that there is no unnecessary talking between helpers, which can take up a lot of usage. If you find yourself burning through usage, both opus 5.5 and fable 5.2 are pretty good at telling you why they are and setting up its own plan for how to reduce that usage without hindering quality. But as far as using fable 5.2 goes, it does an absolutely amazing job on my own game project. It works faster and way more efficiently for me. It catches things that opus 5.5 didn't with its helpers, right away, and tells them to fix it before I have to even give instructions. I'm still early in my testing, but so far fable 5.2 is an amazing orchestrator for handling everything I've been throwing at it without burning usage.

comments.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
comments.body: I'm finding this is pretty important. Fable 5.2 will use its resources to the max if you allow it. I've given mine similar instructions. I tell it to use opus 5.5 on medium at the most for difficult tasks, and sonnet for the rest. And fable 5.2 basically just acts as the director and reviewer and using it this way does an amazing job. I'm running fable 5.2 on medium and so far it's been way more intelligent in how it handles things then opus 5.5 on high was for me

comments.author: Mazapan93
comments.body:
From my projects that ive been working on Opus 5.5 on medium has been pretty good. Mostly because I still prefer a certain degree of control over the end product. However If youre running through credits and hitting limits so fast I think its more of a structure issue than anything else. How much are you having Claude do for you? 

A github repo I was considering using next round: [https://github.com/gamedev-skills/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills](https://github.com/gamedev-skills/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills)

comments.author: viral-architect
comments.body: I had a game I'm working on that I wanted to work on the performance and the visuals of the debris. I told it to ONLY focus on those things. I burned through 1 5 hour session BUT the results were actually noticable improvements with something I did not feel like untangling myself.

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body: On Ultra/Max x20 it seems to be pretty reasonable in terms of usage when used as the orchestrator and told clearly to scope its agents properly.

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body: the director setup is the move yeah. biggest thing is dont let fable re read the whole repo every turn, have it write the plan + what done looks like once, then it only reviews diffs from opus/sonnet. the re reads are what nuke your 5hr window lol. also that 157k vs 89k tokens comment is kinda the real story, fewer tokens per run matters more than the sticker price
